messages.author: 01f6369a4e3b9c88
messages.subject: Clicks and normalisation
parts:
Hi, I'm new here :) After writing a paper with Jerome at the moment, I figured it is time to join the seewave fun. Please bear with me - I am a rubbish R programmer (unfortunately Jerome hasn't ported seewave to SAS or VB.Net, hehe)

My first little project was to write a subsampler. While I'll make it more random in the future, I am pulling out the first second of every minute of recording and I noticed that in some sections of my (underwater) recordings I am getting clicks where the files are joined, despite trying both options to avoid them: the sample attached was created using join=true in pastew. I couldn't get tjoin to work, that actually introduced gaps (is that a hint?).

The second issue is that I don't want the output normalised, but I couldn't quite figure out how to turn that off :)

Anyway, my code is below, I attached my clicky output and the original file (56MB) is here: https://drive.google.com/open?id=0B6U5Ptrx8PA5UThJM2xmRWdib1E

If anyone has any ideas how I can avoid the clicks, that would be awesome! 
Simon


soundfile<-"chopped.wav"
detectsamplerate<-readWave(soundfile, units = c("minutes"), header=TRUE)

#calculates duration and sampling freq
dursec<-detectsamplerate[[4]] /detectsamplerate[[1]]
durmin<-as.integer(dursec/60)-1
freq<-detectsamplerate[[1]]

#duration of the sample (in minutes)
sampdur<-1/60

sampler<-readWave(soundfile,from = 0, to = 0+sampdur, units = c("minutes"))

for(offset in 1:durmin) #loops through each minute
      {loopsamp<-readWave(soundfile, from = offset, to = offset+sampdur, units = c("minutes"))    
       sampler2<-pastew(loopsamp, sampler, f=freq,   join=TRUE )
       sampler<-sampler2}

savewav(sampler, "1secsample_choppedbeforesample.wav", f=48000, rescale=NULL)

messages.author: bfa183f4897a5619
messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Clicks and normalisation
parts:
Hi Simon,

Clicking is very common any time you join two chunks of WAV together like this, because it introduces a discontinuity in the waveform. Depending on your purpose in constructing the waveform out of subsamples, there are a couple of ways to mitigate this.

(1) before joining each subsample to the longer waveform, fade it down at the ends. For instance, for a two-second fade at the beginning and end of each sample you should be able to do something like

loopsamp = fadew(loopsamp, din = 2, dout = 2, frequency = f)

(see the help page for fadew() for some more details)

(2) if you need to come as close as possible to maintaining the wave amplitude throughout, you could run some sort of smoother at the sample transitions after you've constructed the longer waveform.

best,
jesse

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Clicks and normalisation
parts:
Hi Simon and Jesse,

Yes fading might be a good option.

Which value of tjoin did you use? Short values (e.g. 0.001) usually
works better.

Regarding saving without normalisation, the trick is to use the
argument 'rescale' of savewav():

savewav(sampler, "1secsample_choppedbeforesample.wav", f=48000,
rescale=range(sampler)) # if sampler is a matrix as in your code

savewav(sampler, "1secsample_choppedbeforesample.wav",
rescale=range(sampler@left)) # if sampler is a Wave object

HTH

Jerome

parts:
Great!
This warning just tells you that decimal numbers are converted into
integers (to save memory I guess). A dummy example:

> s <- Wave(left=c(0.2,1.6), samp.rate=44100)
Warning message:
In .local(left, ...) : 'bit' not specified, assuming 16bit
> writeWave(s, filename="s.wav")
Warning message:
In writeWave(s, filename = "s.wav") :
channels' data will be rounded to integers for writing the wave file

> s.load <- readWave("s.wav")
> s.load@left
[1] 0 1

HTH

Jerome
